. When the matter was taken up for hearing on 01.12.2023, this Court passed the following order:
When the matter was taken up for hearing, the learned Additional Government Pleader produced the written instructions received from the second respondent.
On going through the same, it is seen that a reference has been made to the proceedings of the District Collector, dated 11.06.2019.

It is also mentioned in the written instructions that the petitioner was paid enhanced compensation of Rs.33,77,172/-
and solatium of Rs.11,63,031/-.
2.The
learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that there is no dispute with regard to the fact that the petitioner was paid the compensation of Rs.33,77,172/- along with solatium.
The learned counsel further contended that the compensation was fixed based on the joint meeting that was headed by the Collector, wherein, it was decided to fix the market value as on 01.04.2012.

The learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner has independently filed an appeal under Section 3(G)(5) of the National Highways Act on 22.10.2018 and this appeal has not been heard and disposed of by the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis District Collector.
A representation was made in this regard by the petitioner on 20.04.2020 and this also did not evoke any response.

3.The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents 1 and 2 and also the learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the National Highways Department shall take specific instructions as to the status of the appeal that was filed by the petitioner on 22.10.2018 before the District Collector under Section 3(G) (5) of the National Highways Act.
4.Post the matter under the same caption on 08.12.2023.

3. When the matter was taken up for hearing today, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents 1 and 2 and the Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the third respondent and learned Central Government Standing Counsel appearing for the fourth respondent clarified this Court that the appeal that was filed by the petitioner dated 22.10.2018 was d e a l t w i t h b y t h e D i s t r i c t C o l l e c t o r / A r b i t r a t o r a n d t h e e n q u i r y w a s https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis attended by the son of the petitioner named Britto Jayasingh and his statement was also recorded.

Based on the same, the final order / Award was passed by the District Collector / Arbitrator on 11.06.2019 by enhancing the compensation and this compensation amount was also paid to the petitioner on 16.03.2020.
Thus, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents have clarified the query that was posed by this Court during the earlier hearing.
4. In view of the above, the relief as sought for by the petitioner cannot be granted by this Court and this Writ Petition is disposed of accordingly.
No costs.
